programmes.name: EIC Accelerator 2026 — Open call (HORIZON-EIC-2026-ACCELERATOR-01)
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, European Commission
programmes.region: EU-level (EU Member States + Horizon Europe Associated Countries)
programmes.page_evidence: The EIC's own Accelerator page describes the live four-step process ("Write your short proposal / Prepare your full proposal / Pitch your innovation / Sign the grant component") and lists 2026 full-proposal batching cut-offs still in the future: "02/09/2026" and "04/11/2026". The FAQ page states "Short proposals are collected for evaluation on the first Tuesday of every month at 17h00 Brussels time".
programmes.cohort_dates: Short proposal: continuous, evaluated first Tuesday of every month. Full proposal cut-offs 2026: 07 Jan, 04 Mar, 06 May, 08 Jul, 02 Sep, 04 Nov.
programmes.cash: Grant up to EUR 2.5M (TRL 6-8), grant-only possible; optional EIC Fund equity EUR 0.5M-10M. 2026 budget EUR 634M.
programmes.terms_dilution: Grant component is fully non-dilutive. Equity component is optional and can be declined (grant-only route).
programmes.hard_blocker: null - no hard legal or eligibility wall found for submitting a short proposal.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No published team-size rule. Work programme explicitly contemplates "one or more natural persons (including individual entrepreneurs)" as applicants, which accommodates a solo founder.
programmes.location_requirement: Establishment in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country is required at grant signature, NOT at short-proposal submission. India is a non-associated third country.
programmes.application_effort: High. Short proposal = 12-page form + pitch deck + video pitch. Full proposal = 20-page form. Realistically 40-80 hours for a first-time applicant. Video pitch is mandatory.
programmes.credits_and_tools: EIC Business Acceleration Services for beneficiaries (corporate/investor introductions, coaching).
programmes.customer_access: Via EIC BAS corporate partnership days; not a customer-acquisition programme per se.
programmes.network_quality: Highest-tier EU deep-tech signal. EIC portfolio is the reference set for European deep tech.
programmes.brand_value: Very high in Europe; the single strongest non-dilutive credential on the continent.
programmes.notes: THIS IS THE HEADLINE FINDING FOR THIS LANE. The EIC FAQ answers the lane's decisive question directly and favourably: "If your company is based in a non-associated third country but intends to establish an SME (including start-ups) or to relocate an existing SME to a Member State or an Associated Country, your company may submit a short proposal as a company from a non-associated third country, but must prove its effective establishment in a Member State or an Associated Country at the time of submission of the full proposal." Secondary sources reading the 2026 work programme also record eligibility for "one or more natural persons (including individual entrepreneurs) or legal entities intending to establish an SME or small mid-cap in a Member State or Associated Country by the time of signing the grant agreement". So: no entity needed to submit Step 1; EU/AC establishment needed only at Step 2 / signature. That converts an apparent hard wall into a sequencing decision. CAVEAT FOR PHASE 2: verify the exact natural-person wording against the EIC Work Programme 2026 PDF (https://eic.ec.europa.eu/document/download/52598755-1351-4b54-b46b-e2682d0a3aec_en?filename=EIC-Work-Programme-2026.pdf) rather than the consultancy summaries. Also note EIC targets TRL 6-8 deep tech with strong emphasis on technological (not purely software/business-model) breakthrough — Supaprod's fit on 'deep tech' is arguable and is the real risk, not eligibility.

programmes.name: EIC Accelerator Challenges 2026
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, European Commission
programmes.region: EU-level (EU Member States + Horizon Europe Associated Countries)
programmes.page_evidence: Same EIC Accelerator page and cut-off calendar as the Open call; 2026 cut-offs 02 Sep and 04 Nov are still ahead.
programmes.cohort_dates: Same six 2026 cut-offs as the Open call.
programmes.cash: Same instrument as Accelerator Open. 2026 Challenges budget EUR 220M, EUR 20-50M per challenge.
programmes.hard_blocker: Not a legal wall, but the five 2026 challenge themes are all outside this company's domain, so no submittable topic exists.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Same as Accelerator Open.
programmes.location_requirement: Same as Accelerator Open.
programmes.application_effort: Same as Accelerator Open.
programmes.customer_access: Challenge owners are the intended adopters, so there is a demand-side pull.
programmes.notes: SECTOR MISMATCH, listed only so it is not silently missed. The five 2026 challenge themes are advanced materials for renewable energy and storage, fusion power plants, biotechnology for regenerating agricultural soils, the European critical raw materials value chain, and climate adaptation. None fits a horizontal AI product-lifecycle SaaS. Route for Supaprod is the Open call, not Challenges.

programmes.name: EIC Pathfinder Challenges 2026
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, European Commission
programmes.page_evidence: The EIC Pathfinder page shows Pathfinder Challenges 2026 with status Open, deadline "28 October 2026", budget "EUR 96 millions", and states eligibility for "single applicants, small and larger consortia (two partners) for EIC Pathfinder Challenges only".
programmes.cohort_dates: Single annual cut-off; projects start after grant agreement.
programmes.cash: Up to EUR 4M grant per project; 2026 Challenges budget EUR 96M (Pathfinder total EUR 262M).
programmes.hard_blocker: An EU/AC legal entity must exist to submit. There is no equivalent of the Accelerator's non-associated-third-country short-proposal carve-out here.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Single legal entity may apply for Challenges (unlike Pathfinder Open). No team-size rule, but evaluation rewards multidisciplinary research teams.
programmes.location_requirement: Applicant must be a legal entity established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
programmes.application_effort: Very high. Full Horizon Europe RIA proposal, typically 100+ hours, needs research-grade novelty framing.
programmes.customer_access: None directly; this is pre-commercial research funding.
programmes.network_quality: European research elite rather than founder network.
programmes.brand_value: High academic/deep-tech credibility, low commercial signal.
programmes.notes: STAGE MISMATCH. Pathfinder funds TRL 1-4 visionary research. Supaprod ships end to end today, which is TRL 8-9 — it is on the wrong side of this instrument. Recorded because it is the only 2026 Pathfinder route still open to a SINGLE entity and because the lane brief asked for Pathfinder explicitly.

programmes.name: EIC Pathfinder Open 2026
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, European Commission
programmes.page_evidence: The EIC Pathfinder page still labels Pathfinder Open 2026 status "Open" while giving a deadline of "12 May 2026", which has passed — the page contradicts itself. I could not resolve it on the authoritative source: the EU Funding & Tenders Portal topic page is a JavaScript single-page app that rendered only the navigation chrome and cookie banner under both WebFetch and headless Playwright (body text returned was the site menu and footer only, no topic status, deadline or eligibility block). No login wall — a rendering failure. Do not record this as CLOSED without loading the portal topic page in a real browser.
programmes.cohort_dates: Single annual cut-off; next cycle expected under the EIC 2027 work programme.
programmes.cash: Up to EUR 4M grant; 2026 Open budget EUR 166M.
programmes.hard_blocker: An EU/AC legal entity must exist to submit, and the default route requires a 3-entity, 3-country consortium.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Default route requires at least 3 independent entities from 3 different Member States/Associated Countries; a single entity may apply in its own right but most funded projects are consortia.
programmes.location_requirement: EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country establishment.
programmes.application_effort: Very high, full RIA proposal.
programmes.notes: Same TRL 1-4 mismatch as Pathfinder Challenges. Also reported to have drawn a record 2,103 proposals in 2026.

programmes.name: EIC Transition 2026 (HORIZON-EIC-2026-TRANSITIONOPEN)
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, European Commission
programmes.page_evidence: The EIC Transition page gives "Deadline for submissions" as 16 September 2026 — still ahead of today — and describes the single 2026 cut-off with no closure notice.
programmes.cohort_dates: Single 2026 cut-off, 16 September 2026. No Challenge calls this year, so only one deadline.
programmes.cash: Up to EUR 2.5M grant at 100% funding rate, plus booster grants up to EUR 50,000. 2026 budget EUR 100M.
programmes.hard_blocker: Proposals must build on results already achieved within an eligible prior EU-funded project (EIC Pathfinder, ERC Proof of Concept, Horizon 2020/Europe RIA, European Defence Fund, Research Infrastructures) at TRL 3-4. Supaprod has no prior EU-funded project result to build on, so the applicant is ineligible on the face of the rules — a genuine eligibility wall, not a preference.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Individual applicants (SMEs, spin-offs, startups, research institutions) or small consortia of max 5 partners are eligible; no team-size rule.
programmes.location_requirement: EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
programmes.application_effort: High, but moot given the prior-project requirement.
programmes.notes: Listed for completeness because the lane brief names Horizon Europe calls open to a single SME, and Transition is one. The prior-EU-project prerequisite is the blocker and cannot be engineered around in this cycle.

programmes.name: EIC Advanced Innovation Challenges — Pilot (Stage 1)
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, European Commission
programmes.page_evidence: "The deadline for submitting your proposal was 26 February 2026 at 17h00 Brussels local time." The page also gives Stage 2 as open only to Stage 1 winners, with an indicative deadline of "18 June 2027 at 17h00 Brussels local time".
programmes.cohort_dates: Stage 1 results indicatively May 2026; Stage 2 indicative deadline 18 June 2027 (winners only).
programmes.cash: Stage 1: EUR 300,000 lump sum for up to nine months. Stage 2: up to EUR 2.5M lump sum for up to 2.5 years. 2026 budget EUR 6M.
programmes.hard_blocker: For this cycle, the Stage 1 intake is over and Stage 2 is winners-only. Structurally an EU/AC legal entity is required to submit.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Stage 1 explicitly accepts "a single legal entity established in a Member State or an Associated Country", including start-ups and SMEs; large companies excluded. No team-size rule.
programmes.location_requirement: Single legal entity established in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
programmes.application_effort: Moderate for an EU instrument — a lump-sum Stage 1 concept, much lighter than a full Horizon proposal.
programmes.customer_access: Demand-driven challenges implies an identified adopter.
programmes.brand_value: New pilot, so brand value is unproven but carries the EIC name.
programmes.notes: WORTH WATCHING FOR THE NEXT EDITION. Structurally the most founder-friendly EIC instrument found in this sweep — single entity allowed, EUR 300k lump sum, a far lighter Stage 1 than the Accelerator. The 2026 pilot drew high interest. Phase 2 should check whether an AIC Stage 1 call reopens under the EIC 2027 work programme, normally published in November.

programmes.name: EIC STEP Scale Up 2026
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EIC Fund, European Commission
programmes.page_evidence: EIC news and the 2026 work programme state the call "remains continuously open on Funding and Tenders portal with evaluation sessions taking place every quarter", with remaining 2026 proposal batching dates of 9 September 2026 and 25 November 2026.
programmes.cohort_dates: Quarterly batching; remaining 2026 dates 9 Sep and 25 Nov 2026.
programmes.cash: EUR 10M-30M equity per company; 2026 budget EUR 300M, plus a separate EUR 100M STEP Scale Up Defence window.
programmes.terms_dilution: EQUITY ONLY — fully dilutive. Does not belong in the non-dilutive lane on its terms, and requires the company to be raising a private round of EUR 50M or above.
programmes.hard_blocker: Stage wall: the instrument exists to co-invest alongside private rounds of EUR 50M+. A pre-revenue private beta is orders of magnitude below the threshold.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed; irrelevant at this stage gate.
programmes.location_requirement: EU Member State or Associated Country establishment.
programmes.application_effort: Investment-grade due diligence process.
programmes.notes: Recorded so the lane is complete and nobody re-discovers it later. Out of scope on both counts: dilutive, and a scale-up stage gate. The exact apply URL should be confirmed in phase 2 — I could not verify a stable slug for the non-defence STEP Scale Up page (the defence variant is at https://eic.ec.europa.eu/eic-funding-opportunities/eic-step-scale-defence_en).

programmes.name: Eurostars 3 — Call 11
programmes.organisation: Eureka Network / European Partnership on Innovative SMEs, co-funded by Horizon Europe
programmes.region: Pan-European + Eurostars partner countries (incl. Canada, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, UK, Israel, Türkiye)
programmes.page_evidence: Read live in a browser. The call page shows "Start Date: 9 July 2026, 12:00 AM CEST / End Date: 10 September 2026, 2:00 PM CEST" with an active "Apply" control, and the body text "You can submit your R&D and innovation project application between 9 July 2026 and 10 September 2026 at 14:00 CET using our project platform (myeurekaproject.org)."
programmes.cohort_dates: Call opened 9 July 2026; deadline 10 September 2026, 14:00 CET.
programmes.cash: Set by each National Funding Body, not by Eureka. Typically 50-70% of eligible costs, commonly EUR 200k-500k per partner.
programmes.hard_blocker: Two walls stack. (1) "The project consortium is led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country" — India is not on the 38-entry Eurostars country list shown on the page. (2) "The project consortium is composed of at least two entities that are independent of one another" from "at least two Eurostars countries". So this needs an incorporated SME in a Eurostars country PLUS a second independent partner in another country. Not reachable solo, pre-incorporation, from Bangalore.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size rule about founders; the binding constraint is entities, not people. A one-person SME can lead if it is an SME in a Eurostars country.
programmes.location_requirement: Lead must be an SME in a Eurostars country; at least one partner from an EU or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Organisations from non-Eurostars countries may participate only by self-funding their own costs.
programmes.application_effort: High — collaborative R&D proposal plus national funding body pre-engagement, and the page warns of additional national eligibility criteria. 60+ hours plus partner search lead time.
programmes.customer_access: Consortium partners can become first customers or channels.
programmes.network_quality: Strong European industrial R&D network, weaker as a founder/investor network.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate; well known to European public funders, largely unknown to US investors.
programmes.notes: The classic 'European entity required' answer for the lane. If the founder ever incorporates in the EU, Call 12 (expected ~March 2027) becomes reachable and the software fit is good. The page's own caution matters: "If you do not meet all our international eligibility criteria, your application will be rejected."

programmes.organisation: ITEA / Eureka Clusters
programmes.page_evidence: I could not read itea4.org directly — my web-search budget was exhausted before I reached it and I did not open it in a browser. programmes.hard_blocker: Consortium requirement plus an entity in a Eureka country; not reachable solo and pre-incorporation.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed; the constraint is consortium composition, not founder count.
programmes.location_requirement: "Project consortia need to have at least two different partners from two different countries, of which one must be a Eureka Member Country and another one either a Eureka Member Country or a Eureka Associated Country."
programmes.application_effort: Very high and long-cycle: Project Outline, then Letter of Intent, then Full Project Proposal five months later, with partner recruitment in between. Not a solo weekend exercise.

programmes.brand_value: Low outside European industrial R&D circles.

Timeline is the reason to record it now: the call opens 15 September 2026, a month from today, and partner-finding is the long pole.

programmes.name: Eureka Innowwide (market feasibility / viability assessment grants)
programmes.organisation: Eureka Network, co-funded by Horizon Europe (European Partnership on Innovative SMEs)
programmes.region: EU + Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye, UK
programmes.page_evidence: Not fetched directly; web-search budget exhausted. Whether a 5th call is live is unresolved and must be read off the Innowwide page.
programmes.deadline: null - could not source a current deadline from the programme page
programmes.cohort_dates: Not established for a 5th call.
programmes.cash: EUR 60,000 grant per project.
programmes.hard_blocker: An EU/associated SME must exist to apply. No consortium is needed, which is unusual and favourable.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed — this funds a company's market-entry study, not a cohort.

programmes.name: EuroHPC AI Factories — Playground Access (AI for Industrial Innovation)
programmes.organisation: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)
programmes.region: EU-level (19 AI Factories + 13 AI Factory Antennas across Europe)
programmes.page_evidence: Read live in a browser. The call page's Details block reads "Status: OPEN", "Reference: AI FOR INDUSTRIAL INNOVATION - PLAYGROUND ACCESS", "Deadline model: Permanent", and the body states "Users can apply any time... access can be granted within two working days" with an active "APPLY NOW" link to https://access.eurohpc-ju.europa.eu/.
programmes.cohort_dates: No cohort. Allocations granted for 1, 2 or 3 months; access within two working days.
programmes.cash: No cash. In-kind GPU hours on EuroHPC systems, free of charge.
programmes.terms_dilution: Zero equity, zero cash, zero IP claim. Pure compute grant.
programmes.hard_blocker: A European SME must exist — the access mode is scoped to "European SMEs and startups". No route for an unincorporated founder or a non-European entity.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Irrelevant — this is an access call assessed on the technical proposal, not on team composition. A one-person SME qualifies.
programmes.location_requirement: "Playground provides quick access to European SMEs and startups." The access-modes page adds "The Industrial Innovation Access modes are open and free-of-charge to AI SMEs (including startups) for innovation purposes." A European legal entity IS required — this is the decisive lane answer here.
programmes.application_effort: Very low for this lane — "a short application explaining the relevance of their proposal (templates are provided)", first-come first-served, no competitive selection, eligibility plus technical assessment only. A few hours.
programmes.credits_and_tools: GPU hours on EuroHPC supercomputers including LUMI and newer AI Factory systems, plus AI Factory expert support.
programmes.network_quality: Technical support network rather than a founder network.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a credential, high as a cost lever.
programmes.notes: THE CHEAPEST WIN IN THIS LANE IF AND ONLY IF AN EU ENTITY EXISTS. No competitive selection, decision in two working days, permanent deadline model. Two sibling modes on the same track — Fast Lane and Large Scale — are a separate row. Nothing here is reachable pre-incorporation, but the moment an EU entity exists this is a same-week action, not a quarterly cut-off.

programmes.organisation: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)

programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not a factor.
programmes.location_requirement: European AI SMEs and startups.

programmes.credits_and_tools: Large GPU allocations plus AI Factory services.

programmes.name: AI-BOOST — AI Challenge Competition (Challenges 1-4)
programmes.organisation: AI-BOOST consortium, funded by the European Union (GA No 101135737), delivered via F6S
programmes.region: EU Member States, Overseas Countries and Territories, and Horizon Europe Associated Countries
programmes.page_evidence: Read live in a browser. The page shows "Challenge 1 and 2 deadline: 25 August 2026 - 17:00 CEST" with an "Apply here to challenge 1 or 2" link, and "Challenge 3 and 4 deadline: 8 September 2026 - 17:00 CEST" with an "Apply here to challenge 3 or 4" link. Both deadlines are ahead of today and no closure notice appears.
programmes.cohort_dates: Spark Phase concept note by 25 Aug (ch. 1-2) or 8 Sep 2026 (ch. 3-4); Advance Phase is a five-month development and validation programme ending in a live demonstration.
programmes.cash: Spark Phase: EUR 28,500 to each of five winners per challenge. Advance Phase: EUR 100,000 final prize per challenge.
programmes.hard_blocker: Scope, not eligibility. All four challenges are narrow and owner-defined: GenAI natural-language mission generator for agricultural robots (Intellimech), agentic AI for automated CAD generation and simulation (SIAD Group), GenAI for enhancing clinical imaging datasets (EUCAIM), and GenAI for automatic test-case generation from crash databases (Siemens). None maps to a product-lifecycle decision platform.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly open to individuals: "Applications may be submitted by individuals, single legal entities, or teams/consortia from academia and industry." A solo founder is expressly contemplated.
programmes.location_requirement: Applicants must be established in an EU Member State, Overseas Countries and Territories, or eligible Associated Countries. Projects must be civil-application only.
programmes.application_effort: Low for Spark Phase — a concept note, perhaps 10-20 hours. Advance Phase is a five-month build commitment.
programmes.customer_access: Direct line to the challenge owner as an adopter.
programmes.brand_value: Moderate within the EU AI ecosystem.
programmes.notes: IMPORTANT AS A PRECEDENT even though this cycle's themes do not fit. AI-BOOST is the clearest example found of an EU-funded scheme that accepts INDIVIDUALS as applicants — no entity needed to submit — which is the exception to this lane's usual rule. The binding constraint is establishment in the EU/OCT/AC, not incorporation. Worth tracking for future challenge rounds, and worth noting for the pattern: EU cascade and prize instruments delivered through F6S are systematically more open to unincorporated applicants than the Horizon Europe mainline.

programmes.name: Apply AI Startup Award 2026
programmes.organisation: European AI Office (European Commission), organised within AI-BOOST, delivered via F6S
programmes.page_evidence: Read live in a browser. The programme page states "Apply by 22 July 2026, 17:00 CEST" and gives a timeline of "Submission Deadline: 22 July 2026 at 17:00 CEST (Brussels time) / Communication of the Top 10 finalists: Mid-September 2026 / Official Award Ceremony (Apply AI Summit): 17 November 2026". The page itself carries no 'closed' notice, and I did not load https://www.f6s.com/apply-ai-startup-award to see whether the submission form still accepts input — that is what blocked a definite answer.
programmes.cohort_dates: Top 10 finalists mid-September 2026; online pitching October 2026; ceremony at the Apply AI Summit 17 November 2026.
programmes.cash: None. "Please note that this is not a cash prize competition." Winners get a main-stage pitch slot, Commission channel coverage, travel costs to Brussels for two representatives, and a trophy.
programmes.hard_blocker: Three walls. (1) "be headquartered in the European Union and be directly majority-owned, meaning more than 50% of the capital is held by entities established in the European Union". (2) "companies must be nominated by national startup associations. Only upon receiving an invitation can candidates complete the application form" — nomination-gated, not open entry. (3) Core business must sit in one of the Apply AI Strategy sectors (healthcare, robotics, manufacturing, defence, mobility, electronic communications, energy, climate, agri-food, cultural/creative, public sector) — a horizontal developer-tools platform is not among them.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed; the gate is company-level.
programmes.location_requirement: EU headquarters plus EU majority ownership.
programmes.application_effort: Low if nominated, impossible if not.
programmes.brand_value: High visibility in EU policy circles, no cash.
programmes.notes: Recorded for the pattern rather than the opportunity: this is the strictest EU-ownership test found in the sweep (EU HQ AND >50% EU-held capital), the kind of clause that would bite a Delaware-parent structure later. Not actionable this cycle on any of three counts.

programmes.name: Frontier AI Grand Challenge
programmes.organisation: European Commission and EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, via AI-BOOST
programmes.page_evidence: Read live in a browser. The page states in its own headline copy: "The FRONTIER AI GRAND CHALLENGE is now closed!" It also records "Submission Deadline: 13 April 2026 at 17:00 CET (Brussel's Time)" and "Results Published: May 2026".
programmes.cohort_dates: Launched 13 Feb 2026, closed 13 Apr 2026, results May 2026.
programmes.cash: No cash. Winner receives Strategic Access to up to 2.5% of overall EuroHPC computing resources for one year, plus AI Factory services.
programmes.hard_blocker: "Eligible participants shall consist of one or more industrial players that are both established in the EU and under EU control", and "All participants must show a history of developing and deploying large-scale AI models (100Bn+ parameters)". Proposals must target models of "at least 400 billion parameters". Comprehensively out of reach.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Irrelevant at this scale.
programmes.location_requirement: Established in the EU and under EU control.
programmes.application_effort: Very high.
programmes.notes: Closed and permanently out of scope. Recorded so it is not re-surfaced by a future sweep as an unexplored EU AI opportunity.

programmes.name: Women TechEU (third edition, 2026-2028)
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council / EISMEA, under the European Innovation Ecosystems work programme of Horizon Europe
programmes.page_evidence: The active-calls page shows the Eligibility Strand opening 1 June 2026 with "Weekly cut-offs every Tuesday at 17:00 CEST; final cut-off 14 June 2027", and the Full Proposal Strand opening 15 July 2026 with submission dates 16 September 2026, 14 January 2027, 1 April 2027 and 8 July 2027.
programmes.cohort_dates: Two-stage: weekly eligibility cut-offs, then four full-proposal cut-offs, first on 16 September 2026.
programmes.cash: EUR 75,000 non-dilutive per selected startup; EUR 12M across 160 startups 2026-2028.
programmes.hard_blocker: Gender eligibility wall. The programme funds "women-led early-stage deep tech startups" and the EIC describes it as "equity-free grants for women founders in deep tech". The founder does not meet the eligibility criterion. This is a published eligibility requirement, not a preference.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Solo-friendly in structure, but the gender criterion is dispositive.
programmes.location_requirement: European startups (EU + Horizon Europe Associated Countries).
programmes.application_effort: Moderate two-stage process.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Personalised business development programme, one-to-one mentoring, training, investor and corporate matchmaking.
programmes.notes: INELIGIBLE — recorded deliberately, not as a candidate, so phase 2 does not spend a verification cycle rediscovering the best-known EUR 75k equity-free EU scheme and reaching the same conclusion. The generous two-stage rolling structure here (weekly eligibility cut-offs) is worth noting as the template EISMEA now uses; watch for a non-gendered sibling instrument under the same EIE work programme.

programmes.name: Open Horizons Project (equity-free grants for women-led deep tech and digital startups)
programmes.organisation: Open Horizons consortium, EISMEA / European Commission
programmes.region: EU Member States + Horizon Europe Associated Countries
programmes.page_evidence: The EISMEA page I read describes only the FIRST call, with a deadline of "21 August 2025, 17:00 CEST", which has passed. Whether a second call is open is unresolved: I did not load https://www.openhorizonsproject.eu itself — the web-search budget was exhausted before I reached it and I did not browse it. The EISMEA page carries no closure notice for the project as a whole.
programmes.cohort_dates: First call only; later call dates not established.
programmes.cash: "Up to EUR 55 000 in equity-free funding" plus mentoring and matchmaking.
programmes.hard_blocker: Gender eligibility wall: "Led by at least one woman in a key executive role (CEO, CTO, or Founder) with minimum 25% ownership." The founder does not meet this.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed beyond the leadership criterion.
programmes.location_requirement: "Based in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe-associated country."
programmes.application_effort: Moderate.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Tailored mentoring, strategic matchmaking, and "opportunities to co-design and test paid pilot projects with major European corporates".
programmes.customer_access: Paid corporate pilots are explicitly on offer — unusually concrete for an EU scheme.
programmes.notes: INELIGIBLE on the same gender criterion as Women TechEU. Recorded because the paid-corporate-pilot mechanic is the most commercially useful design in this lane and is worth watching in case a non-gendered equivalent appears under the same EIE strand.

programmes.name: 28DIGITAL Venture Incubation Program 2026 (formerly EIT Digital Venture Program)
programmes.organisation: 28DIGITAL (EIT Digital successor entity), EIT / European Institute of Innovation and Technology
programmes.region: EU Member States + Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye, Ukraine
programmes.page_evidence: Read live in a browser. Under "How to apply", step 2 reads "Complete the application form" followed by "Application period is closed." Step 3 reads "Applications closing on 9 June 2026 at 17:00 (Brussels time)."
programmes.cohort_dates: Bootcamp, then 12-week online incubation, then Demo Day; Stage 2 Final Prize thereafter.
programmes.cash: EUR 5,000 Growth Package Prize at Stage 1; up to EUR 25,000 at Stage 2.
programmes.terms_dilution: NOT NON-DILUTIVE. The page states: "Important: Selected ventures will commit to providing 28DIGITAL with 5% equity through a SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity)." 5% for EUR 5k-30k is a punishing ratio and disqualifies this on terms alone.
programmes.hard_blocker: Location. Applicants must "reside in or are established in one of the following eligible locations" (EU Member States plus Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye, Ukraine). Residence in Bangalore fails the test.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: The unincorporated-team route requires a minimum of two members: "open to multidisciplinary teams (minimum two members) and early-stage startups incorporated in 2025 or later". Published, but a soft wall in principle since a co-founder could be added.
programmes.location_requirement: Reside in or be established in an EU Member State or one of Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye, Ukraine. Startups must not have been legally established before 1 January 2025.
programmes.application_effort: Moderate.
programmes.credits_and_tools: 12-week online incubation, mentoring, MVP development support, help with EU incorporation.
programmes.customer_access: Demo Day investor jury; limited customer access.
programmes.network_quality: Good European early-stage network; the EIT Digital lineage is real.
programmes.notes: Closed for 2026 and, more importantly, fails the lane's own premise: it takes 5% equity via SAFE, so it is not a non-dilutive scheme despite sitting inside the EIT/EU institutional family. 28DIGITAL holds a Memorandum of Cooperation with EIT for 2025-2027, so a 2027 call is likely — but the equity term is the reason to deprioritise it regardless.

programmes.name: 28DIGITAL Champions (formerly EIT Digital Challenge)
programmes.organisation: 28DIGITAL / EIT Digital
programmes.region: EU Member States + Horizon Europe Associated Countries
programmes.page_evidence: I could not establish the 2026 edition's status from any page. Search results state only that "Applications for 2026 are yet to be launched, but they usually open in late spring or early summer, with the deadline typically at the end of July", and that the programme rebranded from EIT Digital Challenge to 28DIGITAL Champions in late 2025. What blocked me: the web-search budget was exhausted before I could locate and read the live 28DIGITAL Champions call page. Not a login wall.
programmes.deadline: null - no current deadline could be sourced from a programme page
programmes.cohort_dates: Historically applications open late spring / early summer, deadline end of July; 50 finalists pitch to an international investor jury.
programmes.cash: No cash prize in recent editions; winners receive tailored support through the EIT Digital Growth Services Program for international expansion.
programmes.hard_blocker: Traction wall in recent editions: companies must be incorporated in an EU-27 or associated country after 1 January 2015 AND have either annual revenue of at least EUR 500,000 or at least EUR 2 million raised. Supaprod has zero revenue and no external raise, so it fails both limbs on the published thresholds. Confirm whether the rebranded 2026 edition kept these thresholds.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed; the gates are company-level.
programmes.location_requirement: Incorporated in an EU Member State or associated country.
programmes.application_effort: Moderate.
programmes.network_quality: Strong European scaleup and investor network.
programmes.notes: Scaleup-stage instrument. Recorded for completeness of the EIT Digital family; the revenue/funding thresholds are the blocker, not eligibility to apply.

programmes.name: EIT Jumpstarter 2026
programmes.organisation: EIT Community (cross-KIC: EIT Health, EIT Food, EIT RawMaterials, EIT Climate-KIC, EIT Manufacturing, EIT Urban Mobility)
programmes.region: EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS) countries only
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted before I fetched eitjumpstarter.eu and I did not open it in a browser. Search results state "The application deadline for EIT Jumpstarter 2026 is May 17, 2026", extended from an earlier date, closing at 23:59 CEST. Per the binding rule that is a listing-derived date, not page evidence, so the state stays UNKNOWN pending a direct read.
programmes.cohort_dates: Seven-month pre-acceleration programme.
programmes.cash: Up to EUR 10,000 in prizes.
programmes.hard_blocker: Geographic eligibility wall. Applicants must be from EIT RIS-eligible countries — a defined list of EU Member States (Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Spain), EU Outermost Regions, and Associated Countries/territories (Albania, Armenia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine, Türkiye). India is not eligible, and neither are the higher-income EU states.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Designed for early-stage individual innovators; solo-friendly in principle.
programmes.location_requirement: EIT RIS country.
programmes.application_effort: Low-moderate.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Seven months of training and mentoring.
programmes.network_quality: Moderate; strongest in Central and Eastern Europe.
programmes.notes: One of the very few EU programmes that does NOT require an entity to apply — it is explicitly for pre-company innovators. The blocker is purely geographic and is a hard one. Cash is small in any case.

programmes.name: Digital Europe Programme 2026 — DIGITAL-2026-BESTUSE-10 and DIGITAL-2026-SKILLS-10
programmes.organisation: European Commission / HaDEA (European Health and Digital Executive Agency)
programmes.region: EU Member States + Digital Europe associated countries
programmes.page_evidence: I could not read the authoritative source. The EU Funding & Tenders Portal is a JavaScript single-page app: navigating to a topic-details URL in headless Playwright returned only the site menu and footer ("EU Funding & Tenders Portal / Sign in / EN / Home / Funding / Calls for proposals ...") with no call status, deadline or eligibility block, both before and after accepting cookies and on a second navigation. No login wall — a rendering failure. Secondary EC sources (HaDEA news 10 Apr 2026 and digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu) state the calls "opened on 21 April 2026" with a deadline of "1 October 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time".
programmes.cohort_dates: Not a cohort — project grants.
programmes.cash: Topic-dependent; examples cited include EUR 7.8M for AI uptake in health skills, EUR 10M for Safer Internet Centres, EUR 6M at a 100% funding rate for one information-integrity proposal.
programmes.terms_dilution: Non-dilutive grants, typically 50% co-funding, 100% for some topics.
programmes.hard_blocker: Fit rather than eligibility. The 2026 topics are skills, deployment and public-good oriented (digital skills for AI uptake, Safer Internet Centres, information integrity), not product R&D for commercial SaaS. Most also require multi-country consortia and public-interest deliverables.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed; consortium-level instrument.
programmes.location_requirement: Legal entities established in EU Member States or Digital Europe associated countries. A European legal entity IS required to apply.
programmes.application_effort: Very high — full EU consortium proposal with partners, work packages and co-funding. 100+ hours and months of partner assembly.
programmes.notes: The lane brief named Digital Europe explicitly, so it is answered here: yes, a legal entity established in an EU or associated country is required to apply, and in practice a consortium is required too. Not a realistic route for a solo pre-incorporation founder. The useful parts of Digital Europe for this company are its downstream instruments — EDIHs, AI TEFs, and EuroHPC AI Factories — which are separate rows.

programmes.name: Horizon Europe Cluster 4 — Challenge-Driven GenAI4EU Booster (HORIZON-CL4-2026-04-DIGITAL-EMERGING-19)
programmes.organisation: European Commission / HaDEA, AI-Data-Robotics Partnership
programmes.region: EU + eligible countries (EU Member States, Iceland, Norway, Canada, Israel, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom)
programmes.page_evidence: Same blocker as the Digital Europe row: the EU Funding & Tenders Portal topic page is a JavaScript SPA that rendered only navigation chrome and footer under headless Playwright, with no status or deadline block. Listing sources (euro-access.eu, ideal-ist topic tree) give a deadline of "15.04.2026 at 17:00", which has passed, and a call budget of EUR 45,000,000 with roughly EUR 15,000,000 EU contribution per project.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not a cohort — project grants.
programmes.cash: Approximately EUR 15M EU contribution per project.
programmes.hard_blocker: Consortium instrument — collaborative Horizon Europe projects require at least three independent legal entities from three different Member States or Associated Countries, and EUR 15M project sizes are institutional-consortium scale.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not applicable.
programmes.location_requirement: Legal entity established in an eligible country.
programmes.application_effort: Extremely high.
programmes.notes: Answers the lane brief's 'Horizon Europe calls open to a single SME' question in the negative for the AI mainline: GenAI4EU and Cluster 4 Digital calls are consortium instruments. The single-SME routes inside Horizon Europe are the EIC ones — Accelerator, Advanced Innovation Challenges Stage 1, and Pathfinder Challenges — not Cluster 4.

programmes.name: European Innovation Ecosystems (EIE) 2026 CONNECT calls
programmes.organisation: EISMEA / European Commission, Horizon Europe EIE work programme
programmes.page_evidence: I did not read the individual EISMEA call pages — the web-search budget was exhausted after locating them. Search results give: HORIZON-EIE-2026-01-CONNECT-02 (Expanding Investment Ecosystems) and -03 (Scaling up deep tech ecosystems) both with a deadline of 20 January 2026, opened 10 September 2025; and HORIZON-EIE-2026-02-CONNECT-01 (European Startup and Scaleup Hubs pilot) with a deadline of 10 March 2026, opened 12 December 2025, all at 17:00 Brussels local time. Listing-derived, so UNKNOWN stands.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not a cohort — project grants to ecosystem builders.
programmes.cash: Project grants; approximately EUR 1M per project for the Technology Transfer Offices topic, EUR 20M indicative for the Lab to Unicorn initiative.
programmes.hard_blocker: Wrong beneficiary class. These calls fund ecosystem BUILDERS — accelerators, investment networks, university hubs, technology transfer offices — not individual startups. A startup is a downstream beneficiary of these projects, never the applicant.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not applicable.
programmes.location_requirement: EU or Associated Country legal entities, usually in consortia.
programmes.application_effort: Very high.
programmes.notes: Recorded so the EIE strand is explicitly closed out. Its startup-facing outputs are separate schemes — Women TechEU and Open Horizons are both EIE-funded — which is where the founder-relevant money actually surfaces. Also under this strand: the Lab to Unicorn initiative and the European Startup and Scaleup Hubs, both part of the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy, worth monitoring for downstream open calls that startups CAN enter.

programmes.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) — Test Before Invest and free SME services
programmes.organisation: European Commission (Digital Europe Programme), delivered by around 100 national and regional hubs
programmes.region: EU Member States + Digital Europe associated countries (83 EDIHs funded, 102 with recognised status)
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted before I fetched the EDIH catalogue. There is also no single application form: each hub runs its own intake, so 'open' is a per-hub question that cannot be answered from one page. Search results state the services "are mostly publicly funded and therefore typically free of charge for companies", that Test Before Invest projects "typically range from EUR 30,000 to EUR 40,000 and are fully funded by the European Commission", and that the 2026-2029 programme will deliver "over 3,000 engagements, 1,100 'Test Before Invest' projects".
programmes.cohort_dates: Continuous intake, per hub.
programmes.cash: No cash to the company. In-kind services valued around EUR 30,000-40,000 per Test Before Invest project, fully funded by the Commission.
programmes.terms_dilution: Fully non-dilutive, no equity, no repayment.
programmes.hard_blocker: An EU or associated-country company must exist. "Eligible for funding are companies and public institutions from EU Member States and associated countries."
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not a factor — hubs serve companies, and a one-person SME qualifies.
programmes.location_requirement: EU Member State or Digital Europe associated country establishment. A European legal entity is required — this is the decisive lane answer for EDIH.
programmes.application_effort: Very low — a conversation with a local hub and a short service request. Hours, not weeks.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Test Before Invest (access to experimentation and testing facilities, notably AI services), training and skills development, support in finding financing, and networking.
programmes.customer_access: Regional SME and public-sector networks; hubs often broker pilots.
programmes.network_quality: Regional and practical rather than prestigious.
programmes.notes: The single lowest-friction non-dilutive support in the whole lane, and the first thing to switch on the day an EU entity exists. Choice of hub follows the country of incorporation. In phase 2, if an incorporation jurisdiction is under consideration, check which EDIHs there have a reinforced AI focus — the 2026-2029 round explicitly funds 'EDIHs with reinforced AI focus'.

programmes.name: AI Testing and Experimentation Facilities (AI TEFs) — sectorial open calls
programmes.organisation: European Commission (Digital Europe Programme), four sectorial TEF consortia (agri-food, manufacturing, health, smart cities)
programmes.region: EU Member States + Digital Europe associated countries
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted before I could fetch the TEF pages, and each TEF runs its own rolling open calls so status is per-facility rather than per-programme. Search results state TEF-Health "currently has two active Open Calls for subsidized testing, validation, and certification services", that cascade grants run "EUR 50K-200K per SME" against roughly EUR 220M total TEF investment 2022-2027, and that applicants "must be a start-up or SME according to EU SME criteria (turnover, balance, FTE and ownership), profit-making, active and privately owned".
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling per facility.
programmes.cash: Cascade grants typically EUR 50,000-200,000, plus subsidised testing and validation services.
programmes.hard_blocker: Sector fit is the practical wall: the four TEFs are agri-food, manufacturing, healthcare, and smart cities and communities. A horizontal product-lifecycle platform has no natural home unless it is deliberately framed for one vertical.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not a factor.
programmes.location_requirement: EU SME criteria plus EU or associated-country establishment. A European legal entity is required.
programmes.application_effort: Low to moderate — cascade calls are deliberately lighter than mainline EU calls.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Physical and virtual testing environments, regulatory sandboxes, reference datasets, expert support.
programmes.notes: Worth a phase-2 scan only if a vertical framing is acceptable. The EU-entity requirement applies. Related and worth checking on the same pass: the AI-on-Demand Platform open call (up to EUR 60,000, run via F6S) for mature AI providers to integrate and deploy solutions on the AI-on-Demand Platform — I saw the headline but could not verify its deadline or eligibility before the search budget ran out.

programmes.name: Cascade funding / Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) open calls
programmes.organisation: Various Horizon Europe and Digital Europe funded consortia; aggregated at the Cascade Funding Hub
programmes.page_evidence: The Cascade Funding Hub's August 2026 page was read and lists eleven live open calls with deadlines, including "AI-BOOST - AI Challenge Competition (Challenges 1 & 2)", EUR 128,500 total, deadline 25/08/2026, and "HEDGE-IoT - OC#2", EUR 60,000 maximum, deadline 25/08/2026. The aggregator is open and current; individual call states must still be verified per call.
programmes.cohort_dates: Continuous stream of independent calls, typically with 2-4 month windows.
programmes.cash: Typically EUR 20,000-200,000 per beneficiary.
programmes.hard_blocker: None at the channel level; individual calls vary and most require an SME.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Varies by call. AI-BOOST expressly accepts individuals; most others require an SME.
programmes.location_requirement: Varies by call; almost always EU or Associated Country establishment, though AI-BOOST's individual route shows 'establishment' can mean residence rather than incorporation.
programmes.application_effort: Low per call — cascade calls are deliberately "faster, smaller, and less bureaucratic than many direct EU programmes". Often 10-25 hours.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Call-dependent; often includes technical support and infrastructure access.
programmes.customer_access: Often a named challenge owner or adopter.
programmes.notes: CHANNEL ROW, not a single programme — recorded because it is the highest-yield place to hunt in this lane and because the August 2026 crop was dominated by cybersecurity, bioeconomy, agri-food and IoT, none of which fits. The value is the monthly refresh: phase 2 should treat cascadefunding.eu (plus eucalls.net and kaila.eu) as a recurring watch rather than a one-time check, filtering for AI/software horizontals and for the rarer calls that accept individuals rather than SMEs.

programmes.name: EUIPO SME Fund 2026 (Ideas Powered for Business)
programmes.organisation: European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), a European Commission initiative
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted before I fetched the EUIPO page. Search results state the fund runs "from 2 February 2026 to 4 December 2026" or until funds are exhausted, and critically that "Voucher 1 (IP Scans) and Voucher 2 (Trade marks and Designs) are unavailable for new applications as funds have been exhausted due to the high number of requests received. However, you can still apply for Voucher 3 (Patents) and Voucher 4 (Community Plant Varieties)." That partial-exhaustion claim is exactly the kind of state that must be confirmed on the EUIPO page itself.
programmes.cohort_dates: First come, first served throughout 2026 until each voucher's credit is spent.
programmes.cash: Reimbursement vouchers: up to 90% of IP scan costs (Voucher 1), up to 75% of national, EU and regional trade mark and design application fees (Voucher 2), plus patent and plant variety vouchers.
programmes.hard_blocker: An EU-established SME must exist. No route for a non-EU or unincorporated applicant.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not a factor.
programmes.location_requirement: EU-established SME. A European legal entity is required — the decisive lane answer for EUIPO.
programmes.application_effort: Very low — a voucher application, then reimbursement claims. A few hours.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Covers EU trade mark filing costs, which matters for a product name.
programmes.brand_value: None as a credential; purely a cost saving.
programmes.notes: Only becomes live post-incorporation in the EU, and the trade mark voucher — the one that would matter for the Supaprod name — is reported already exhausted for 2026. Note the pattern for planning: this fund reliably exhausts its trade mark credit mid-year, so a 2027 filing plan should target the February reopening.

programmes.name: Enterprise Europe Network (EEN)
programmes.organisation: European Commission / EISMEA, delivered by around 600 partner organisations
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted. There is also no single application: EEN is a network of local contact points, each with its own intake, so state is per-office. Search results state "The services of the Enterprise Europe Network (EEN) are available to SMEs free of charge" and that the network "is active in more than 60 countries worldwide", but do not resolve whether a non-EU company can be served.
programmes.cohort_dates: No cohort; continuous advisory.
programmes.cash: None. Advisory services only.
programmes.hard_blocker: None established. Whether a non-EU applicant can be served was not resolved and is the open question.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not a factor.
programmes.location_requirement: Primarily EU and associated-country SMEs, but the network operates in 60+ countries and the eligibility of a non-EU applicant was not established. Worth one phase-2 question to an Indian or German EEN contact point.
programmes.application_effort: Minimal — contact a local office.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Free advice on cross-border operation, partner search, EU funding navigation, and access to the EEN partnering database.
programmes.customer_access: The EEN partnering database is a genuine cross-border business-partner matching tool.
programmes.network_quality: Broad but shallow; institutional advisors rather than operators.
programmes.notes: Not funding, and the lane brief named it, so it is answered: EEN is a free advisory network, not a grant scheme. Its practical use here is as a cheap intelligence channel — an EEN advisor in a candidate incorporation country is the fastest way to get authoritative answers on national co-funding rates for Eurostars and ITEA, which are the numbers no aggregator gets right.

programmes.name: Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs (SMP-COSME-2026-EYE)
programmes.organisation: European Commission / EISMEA, Single Market Programme (COSME strand)
programmes.region: EU + participating countries (45 countries listed by the programme)
programmes.page_evidence: The programme site presents an active "Apply now" control and states the programme is for people "firmly planning to set up their own business or have already started one within the last three years", with "No fees to participate in the EYE!" No deadline or closure notice is shown — it operates continuously via local contact points.
programmes.cohort_dates: Continuous. Exchanges of 1-6 months arranged individually with a host entrepreneur abroad.
programmes.cash: A monthly financial contribution toward travel and subsistence, set per host country. Not a business grant.
programmes.hard_blocker: Likely residence wall: the 'new entrepreneur' must be a permanent resident of a participating country. Residence in Bangalore is very likely disqualifying, and this single fact decides the row.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Built for individuals. The most explicitly solo-friendly instrument in this lane.
programmes.location_requirement: Permanent residence in one of the 45 participating countries.
programmes.application_effort: Low — an online profile and business plan, plus matching with a host.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Placement with an experienced entrepreneur abroad.
programmes.network_quality: Variable; depends entirely on the host match.
programmes.notes: Recorded because it is the rare EU scheme that needs NO entity to apply and explicitly serves people "firmly planning to set up their own business" — precisely the founder's status. It is a mobility fellowship, not product funding, and a months-long placement abroad is a poor fit for someone shipping to a mid-September launch. The parallel SMP-COSME 2026 calls (EYE consortium call closed 21 April 2026; Tourism SMEs; Agri-food Biotech closed 2 June 2026) fund the intermediary organisations, not entrepreneurs, and are not candidates.

programmes.name: EIC Scaling Club 2.0
programmes.organisation: European Innovation Council, Business Acceleration Services
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted. Search results state the EIC launched a CSA call for an operator of "EIC Scaling Club 2.0" on 22 May 2026, which "should support a minimum of 70 deep tech companies", and that "Deep tech companies can express their interest in joining the Club by filling out a survey". Whether that expression-of-interest survey is live between operator contracts is exactly what is unresolved.
programmes.deadline: null - no deadline could be sourced; membership is by rolling expression of interest
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling cohorts; 72 companies joined in the October 2024 intake.
programmes.cash: None. Growth-capability support, peer and partner networking, investor outreach.
programmes.hard_blocker: Stage and thematic gates: members are selected on "potential to build world-class businesses" in named domains (Agri & Food Tech, Batteries & Energy Storage, Cardiovascular Therapies, Clean Fuels & Hydrogen, New Biotech Platforms, New Space). A pre-revenue horizontal software product is outside both the stage and the domain list.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not addressed.
programmes.location_requirement: European deep tech companies.
programmes.application_effort: Low — an expression-of-interest survey.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Bespoke growth support, peer learning, corporate and investor introductions.
programmes.network_quality: High — the EIC's curated scale-up cohort.
programmes.notes: Low-cost to try (a survey, not an application) but the published domain list excludes horizontal software. Recorded mainly to close out the EIC Business Acceleration Services family, whose other services are reserved for EIC beneficiaries and Seal of Excellence holders — downstream of winning an EIC grant, not an independent route.

programmes.name: Innovation Radar Prize
programmes.organisation: European Commission (DG CNECT), co-organised with Dealflow.eu
programmes.page_evidence: Not read directly — the web-search budget was exhausted. Search results describe the 11th edition (November 2025, Lisbon, 12 innovators across three categories including 'AI & Digital Intelligence') but surface no 2026 edition dates. The mechanism is also not open entry: "Intelligence gathered by the Innovation Radar is used to identify innovators who can then compete for the prize."
programmes.deadline: null - no current edition dates could be sourced
programmes.cohort_dates: Annual, typically an autumn ceremony.
programmes.cash: Recognition, pitch preparation support and market-ambition support rather than a headline cash prize.
